source_text: Conuersus ibidem ad discipulos (uae\' dicit auctori scan. dalorum: expedisse ei, si natus non fuisset aut si molino saxo ad collum deligato praecipitatus esset in profundum, quam unum ex illis modicis utique discipulis eius scandalizasset. aestima, quale supplicium comminetur ille. nec enim! alius ulciscetur scandalum discipulorum eius. agnosce igitur et iudicem et illo adfectu pronuntiantem de cura suorum, quo et creator retro: qui tetigerit uos, ac si pupillam oculi mei tangat. idem sensus eiusdem est. peccantem fratrem iubet corripi; quod qui non fecerit, utique deliquit, aut ex odio uolens fratrem in delicto perseuerare aut ex acceptione personae parcens ei: habes Leuiticum: non odies fratrem tuum in animo tuo, traductione traduces proximum tuum, utique et fratrem, et non sumes propter illum delictum. nec mirum, si ita docet qui pecora quoque fratris tui, si errantia in uia inueneris, prohibet despicias, quominus ea reducas fratri, nedum ipsum sibi. sed et ueniam des fratri in te delinquenti iubet, etiam septies. parum plane. plus est enim apud creatorem, qui nec modum statuit, in infinitum pronuntians: fratris malitiae memor ne sis, nec petenti eam praestes mandat, sed et non petenti. non enim dones offensam uult, sed obliuiscaris. Lex leprosorum quantae sit interpretationis erga species ipsius uitii et inspectationis summi sacerdotis, nostrum erit scire, Marcionis, morositatem legis opponere, ut et hic Christum aemulum eius adfirmet, praeuenientem sollemnia legis etiam in curatione decem leprosorum, quos tantummodo ire iussos, ut se ostenderent sacerdotibus, in itinere purgauit, sine tactu iam et sine uerbo, tacita potestate et sola uoluntate.
pass_a_gloss: Having turned there to the disciples, he says to the author of scandals: it would have been better for him if he had not been born or if with a millstone of rock having been tied to his neck he had been thrown into the deep, than that he scandalized one of those little disciples of his; estimate what kind of punishment he threatens; for no other will avenge the scandal of his disciples; recognize therefore both the judge and the one pronouncing about the care of his own, with that same affection with which also the creator formerly: whoever touches you, touches as it were the pupil of my eye; the same sense is of the same one; he commands to rebuke a sinning brother; which whoever does not do, certainly has failed, either from hatred willing that the brother persist in the sin or from acceptance of person sparing him; you have Leviticus: you shall not hate your brother in your soul, by a translation you shall translate your neighbor, certainly also the brother, and you shall not take for him the sin; and no wonder, if thus he teaches who also forbids that you despise the livestock of your brother, if you find them straying in the way, lest you reduce them to the brother, not to mention himself; but also he commands to give forgiveness to the brother sinning against you, even seven times; plainly not enough; for it is more with the creator, who does not set a limit, pronouncing to infinity: be not mindful of the malice of the brother, and do not give to the one asking it, but also not to the one not asking; for he does not want you to give offense, but to forget; the law of the lepers, how great an interpretation it is with respect to the species of that vice and the inspection of the high priest, will be ours to know, Marcion, to oppose the morosity of the law, so that even here Christ may be affirmed as the rival of the same, anticipating the solemnities of the law even in the healing of the ten lepers, whom only he commanded to go, so that they might show themselves to the priests, on the way he purified, without touch now and without word, with silent power and alone with will.

pass_b_english: He turns there to the disciples and says to the author of scandals: it would have been better for him if he had not been born, or if with a millstone of rock tied to his neck he had been thrown into the deep, than that he scandalized one of those little disciples of his; estimate what kind of punishment he threatens, for no other will avenge the scandal of his disciples. Recognize therefore both the judge and the one pronouncing about the care of his own, with that same affection with which the Creator also spoke formerly: 'Whoever touches you touches as it were the pupil of my eye' (Zechariah 2:8); the same sense is of the same One. He commands that a sinning brother be rebuked; whoever does not do this has certainly failed, either from hatred wanting the brother to persist in the sin, or from partiality sparing him. You have Leviticus: 'You shall not hate your brother in your soul; by a translation you shall translate your neighbor, certainly also the brother, and you shall not take sin on his account' (Leviticus 19:17). And no wonder, if he teaches thus who also forbids you to despise the livestock of your brother, if you find them straying in the way, lest you lead them back to the brother, not to mention the brother himself. But he also commands you to give forgiveness to the brother sinning against you, even seven times; plainly not enough. For there is more with the Creator, who does not set a limit, pronouncing to infinity: 'Do not be mindful of the malice of the brother, and give to the one asking, but also to the one not asking' (cf. Matthew 5:42; Luke 6:30); for he does not want you to give offense, but to forget. The law of the lepers, how great an interpretation it is with respect to the species of that vice and the inspection of the high priest, will be ours to know, Marcion, to oppose the morosity of the law, so that even here Christ may be affirmed as the rival of the same, anticipating the solemnities of the law even in the healing of the ten lepers, whom he only commanded to go, so that they might show themselves to the priests; on the way he purified them, without touch now and without word, with silent power and will alone.
